title: UPDATE: Hugging Face Introduces $CARBON Token to Incentivize Community Development of DNA Models
summary:
A new cryptocurrency-based incentive system has been launched to fund and coordinate the open-source development of genomic AI tools. The $CARBON token, released by the team behind the Carbon-X model, operates on the Ethereum blockchain and allows users to acquire discounted credits for DNA data filtering and training runs by burning tokens. In return, contributors can earn the token by providing improved DNA filters, sequence mixtures, or evaluation metrics for the genomic project.

The framework is intended to support the ongoing improvement of Carbon-X, a 14B parameter model that allows researchers to query genetic sequences using natural language. The model was developed by mid-training a Qwen3-14B base on 300B tokens of interleaved DNA and text data. To address questions about the token's implementation and utility, the team scheduled a virtual Q&A session for Oct. 28 at 4 p.m. EST.

selectedTweets.text:
This week, we're introducing an experimental coordination layer for open genomic foundation model work around Carbon and Carbon-X.

It starts as a lightweight surface for community runs. The mechanics are built so it can support broader use if the public outputs keep improving. It plugs into existing training and evaluation workflows without changing how production models are released or used.

- Burn the token to get discounted credits for community training runs, DNA data filtering jobs, and evaluation that follow the staged functional mixtures we used. Creator fees go to public data work, open recipes, and an open bounty pool, in addition to my personal share.

- Contribute a useful DNA filter, sequence mixture, or evaluation improvement and get paid in the token. Accepted work is released with the existing models and demo materials.

- Companies that need production scale training continue at normal rates. Builders who want discounted capacity for public ablations buy and burn the token. Demand tracks actual use of the open resources.

If the public outputs stop advancing useful genomic data or models we shut the layer down. If they continue to improve data quality and model efficiency the coordination can expand.

Ethereum gives the clearest path for integration with existing open model workflows.
Contract: 0x20ec75adc91aa92ec97a2f419fd6829c3123b8bf

Let’s see what the community builds!

selectedTweets.bestBit: Carbon-X outperforms all open language models we evaluated on five benchmarks of DNA understanding and generation. This is a 27-point improvement over Qwen3-14B
selectedTweets.text:
Frontier labs are advancing the capabilities in AI for biology but preventing the good guys (scientists, academia, non-profits, health agencies,...) to use, study and understand it with widespread but shallow guardrails that the bad guys are bypassing easily (blocked me to proofread this tweet for example 😅). 

This will automatically create massive assymetry and risks in the coming years, just like in cybersecurity, especially now that frontier labs are building wet labs (HF cybersecurity scenario for biology when?).

This is why we created Carbon-X, the best open-source DNA model by midtraining Qwen3-14B on 300B tokens of DNA, English and interleaved data.  We also used a hybrid tokenizer that tokenizes English with BPE and DNA with a 6-mer tokenizer.

As a result, Carbon-X outperforms all open language models we evaluated on five benchmarks of DNA understanding and generation. This is a 27-point improvement over Qwen3-14B, showing how much a  language model can gain from DNA training. It is also API frontier level at 1,800x less cost than GPT 6.1 Sol!

We hope Carbon-X helps researchers explore DNA in new ways. Releasing it openly means anyone can study its capabilities, limitations, and risks. Let's make the AI biology frontier open-source to make it safe and impactful for the whole world (not just a few companies).

selectedTweets.text:
While I was writing this, my AI assistant got cut off by a bio safety filter. It was summarizing my own team's notes on the model we released today 😅

Frontier labs are moving fast into biology but the scientists and clinicians who'd get the most out of these models are unfortunately the ones running into walls like this one (and every day).

So we partnered with TIGEM (Telethon Institute of Genetics and Medicine), Naple "Federico II" University and Zhongguancun Academy to train Carbon-X.

Carbon-X is an open 14B model that reads raw DNA and talks about it in plain English. On our DNA benchmarks it scores 67%, vs 61% for Claude Opus 5.5 and 50% for Gemini 4 Argon, and its within a point of GPT-6.1 Sol at about 1000x lower cost.

We kept human and animal viruses out of the training data. The weights are open and the model runs on hardware accessible to academia (a laptop).

One example from the blog: give frontier models an 8kb stretch of the NF1 gene with a mutation at a splice site. Most of them call it benign, refuse, or run out of tokens. Carbon-X says pathogenic, because the mutation breaks the splice site.

This century, biology may be where AI matters most. We want to get there with the safety work done in the open and every lab in the world able to build on it. Go try it, and tell us what you find.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Mid-trained on 300B tokens of interleaved DNA and text, followed by SFT (without distillation!) and RL.
selectedTweets.text:
Today we're releasing Carbon-X, a 14B model that brings DNA and natural language together for the first time 🧬

1. Beats every open language model we tested across DNA benchmarks. Within a point of GPT-6.1 Sol at >1,000× lower inference cost.

2. Mid-trained on 300B tokens of interleaved DNA and text, followed by SFT (without distillation!) and RL.

3. A new hybrid tokenizer encodes DNA using ~3× fewer tokens than BPE.

4. Gives other models a DNA specialist subagent: Kimi K3 gains 11.1 points when it consults Carbon-X.

5. Runs locally on a laptop with llama.cpp. Apache 2.0. Your DNA stays on your hardware.

Model: https://t.co/7wBE7WUVp1
